_comment: AM peak with the Kennedy loaded, for chi-loop-urban. Same 600 s x 9 =
5400 s = 54,000 tick span as profiles-am.json, so the horizon is
unchanged and the last three slices are still the drain.
WHY THIS EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS NOT A GLOBAL SCALE: the run report says
the freeway carries 38% of travel with p99 density at 69% of critical,
while the arterial grid is already at 235% of critical at the tail. A
uniform lift multiplies the arterial strandings (1,021 of them) and
tells you nothing new. This targets the corridor that has headroom.
The shape matters as much as the level. profiles-am.json assigns every
interior mainline injection the `freight` curve, which tops out at 0.90
and never reaches 1.00 -- and those interior injections ARE the Kennedy
fill (the ramp block relocates boundary volume onto Armitage/North/
Division/Ohio-like mainline points). So the corridor with headroom was
the one whose arrival curve was deliberately peak-shaved. `kennedy-am`
holds 1.00 for three consecutive slices: a 10-minute peak cannot build
Fractions are napkin-anchored diurnal shapes, NOT calibrated Chicago
counts (ADR-0028). Do not quote them as counts.

assign._why: The Kennedy's interior mainline injections are what actually fills it. This rule MUST precede the generic kind=interior rule below: first match wins, so ordering it after would leave these flows on `freight` while the rule still fired on other Kennedy flows -- check_all_rules_fired would pass and the corridor would stay peak-shaved.
The boundary portal remainder on the same corridor: whatever --ramp-share did not relocate. It gets the same shape and level, or the corridor arrives in two different curves.
Residents leaving downtown towers are largely counter-peak: they are already in the core, so they are not what fills the inbound expressways.
Interior injections on every OTHER corridor keep the freight mix and its earlier, flatter peak. Unchanged from profiles-am.json -- this is the control side of the comparison.
